item.title: Crusoe Raises Over $3 Billion in Funding at $30 Billion Valuation
item.description: Crusoe, a cloud-computing provider and data center developer doing business with OpenAI, Microsoft Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc., has raised over $3 billion in a funding round that values the startup at roughly $30 billion, according to people familiar with the situation.

item.title: Asia Stocks to Gain as Fed Bets Cool, Dollar Drops: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were poised to rise Friday, tracking gains on Wall Street as investors pared bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike this month. The yen held its biggest gain in over a month and oil rose.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 4
item.description: Oil headed for its biggest weekly gain since July as renewed US-Iran hostilities heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: India Launches Rocket in Boost to Space Ambitions After Failures
item.description: India’s space program notched a much-needed success with a rocket launch on Friday, after two consecutive failures of another launcher that had long served as its workhorse rocket.

item.title: FBI Investigating Possible Exposure of Millions of American IDs
item.description: The FBI is investigating a potential breach of an ID verification company that may have exposed scans of millions of Americans’ driver’s licenses, a bureau spokesperson told Bloomberg News on Thursday.

item.title: Korea’s Financial Labor Union to Strike Against Relocation Plans
item.description: South Korea’s financial industry union plans to strike to protest the government’s push to relocate public institutions out of Seoul, escalating opposition to President Lee Jae Myung’s drive to spread economic activity beyond the capital.

item.title: Anthropic Executive Doesn’t Want to ‘Buy Market Share’ With Price Cuts
item.description: The Claude maker is competing with more affordable options from rivals

item.title: SEC Moves to Nix Rule on Adviser Political Donations
item.description: Investment advisers would no longer be prohibited from offering services to public pension funds if they made recent political donations to state and local elected officials, the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a proposed rule change Thursday.

item.title: Australia’s Battered Bonds Have Reasons to Rebound, Funds Say
item.description: Australia’s bonds, caught up in the global fixed-income selloff, have seen their yields rise more than any of their peers in the past month, despite arguments that the country’s finances are in much better shape.

item.title: Los Angeles Schools Ban Student Use of AI Tools on District Devices
item.description: The Los Angeles Unified School District is barring students from using generative AI tools on district devices as part of a broader push to reduce screen time in the classroom.

item.title: Meet the Biggest Ad Buyer in the Podcasting Industry
item.description: BetterHelp is the top podcast advertiser of all time. Since 2023, the talk therapy provider has spent $242 million on ads in the space, according to one firm’s estimates

item.title: Adobe Names Chakravarthy CEO, While Other Contender Departs
item.description: Adobe Inc. named Anil Chakravarthy, the leader of its marketing and analytics software business, as its next chief executive officer, thrusting the company veteran into a challenging competition with artificial intelligence upstarts.

item.title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Has Fumbled at Communicating AI Benefits
item.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman says top artificial intelligence developers have fumbled at communicating the benefits of the technology, leaving the industry vulnerable to growing backlash from communities around the world.

item.title: Wine Distributor Stephen Burton Gets Prison Term in Rare Vintage Scam
item.description: The founder of a London wine-distribution business was sentenced in the US to six years in prison for orchestrating a scam that cost investors almost $100 million and was based on bottles of rare vintages that didn’t exist.

item.title: Smart Ring Maker Oura Files for US IPO as Revenue Surges
item.description: Health and fitness ring-maker Oura Inc. filed for an initial public offering, showing soaring revenue as well as increasing losses.

item.title: IMF Mulls Opening Caracas Office as Venezuela Engagement Deepens
item.description: The International Monetary Fund is considering opening a local office in Venezuela, establishing permanent representation in the country for the first time in years, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: T-Mobile CEO Gopalan Is Banking on Home Internet, AI for Growth
item.description: As he nears his one-year anniversary as T-Mobile US Inc.’s chief executive officer, Srini Gopalan is counting on growth in businesses such as home internet and artificial intelligence to help buoy a languishing share price.

item.title: Planet Labs Eyes Data-Center Monitoring Expansion as It Looks Beyond Defense
item.description: Planet Labs PBC is in discussions to provide its satellite-imaging services to help monitor data centers, the company’s chief financial officer said, as it looks beyond the defense sector for expansion.

item.title: Industry Urges SEC to Keep Existing Rules for Novel ETFs
item.description: As the regulator mulls next steps, it’s worth looking at how all of this played out in South Korea

item.title: Public Storage Readies Inaugural Canadian Dollar Bond Sale
item.description: Public Storage, a real estate investment trust that owns storage units, is looking to sell around C$500 million ($363 million) of bonds, its first note offering in the currency, after completing the purchase of a group of Canadian properties.

item.title: Crusoe Signs Roughly $13 Billion AI Cloud Deal With Jane Street
item.description: Crusoe, a data center upstart with contracts to supply AI computing power to the likes of Meta Platforms Inc. and Oracle Corp., has signed a cloud contract with trading firm Jane Street Group valued at around $13 billion, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: South Africa’s Kganyago Sees Room for Caution on Rate Moves
item.description: South Africa’s central bank chief Lesetja Kganyago said policymakers can afford to respond cautiously to the aftereffects of inflation shocks such as higher oil prices caused by the Iran war and a looming drought.

item.title: OpenAI Rolls Out GPT-6 Astra Model With Cyber Guardrails
item.description: OpenAI is releasing a new generation of its technology called GPT-6 that the company is positioning as a key milestone in its decade-long push to build so-called artificial general intelligence.

item.title: Elite Public High Schools To Get a Taste of Trump’s College Crusade
item.description: The Trump administration is scrutinizing some of the country’s most elite public high schools over whether their admissions practices discriminate based on race.

item.title: Dollar Falls to Weakest Since May on Waller Comments, Yen Surge
item.description: The dollar sank to the lowest level since May after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller noted progress on inflation and as the yen surged against its major counterparts.

item.title: Pentagon Says Its Anthropic Ban Is On, Despite Lutnick Remarks
item.description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said Anthropic PBC has resolved its long-running issues with the Trump administration but a top Pentagon official begs to differ.

item.title: Chicago Projects $882 Million Budget Gap on Bond, Pension Costs
item.description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson is projecting an $882 million budget deficit for 2027, even as his administration continues to seek ways to close this year’s shortfall, underscoring the financial pressures facing the third-largest US city.

item.title: NYC Transit Agency Prepares $785 Million Mansion Tax Bond Sale
item.description: New York City’s transit network is planning to offer $785 million of debt backed by a levy on sales of luxury real estate.

item.title: Carney Says He’s Open to US Pact if Auto, Steel Terms Are Competitive
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said a trade deal with the US is still possible, but only if the terms keep Canadian automotive and steel operations competitive.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI Hit by Service Outages for AI Models
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic PBC and SpaceXAI were hit by outages on Thursday, according to user reports and company status pages, disrupting customers of three of the leading US AI model makers.
